description.fun: Klink is a pair of interlocking gears that spin around each other to make the energy they need to live. The two gears are a fixed pair, closer than twins, and bounce off any other gear that tries to mesh with them. Turn it any way you like and it still seems to have a face. Klink are even suspected of inspiring ancient people's invention of the first gears.
description.guide: Klink is a Steel-type Pokémon made of two interlocking gears that generate energy by spinning together. It evolves into Klang, then Klinklang.
description.tagline: Two gears closer than twins, spinning to stay alive.

description.fun: Klang shows its feelings by changing which way it spins, and when it's angry it spins faster. In battle it fires its minigear at foes at high speed, a risky move, since it's said to be in serious danger if the gear doesn't come back. Many companies in Galar use Klang as their logo, as it's seen as the symbol of industrial technology. Even so, it was once named the least-searched Pokémon on Pokémon.com's Pokédex.
description.guide: Klang is the evolved form of Klink, a Steel-type Pokémon made of a big gear and a minigear. It communicates by changing the direction it spins. It evolves into Klinklang.
description.tagline: A spinning gear that Galar's companies love to use as a logo.

description.fun: Klinklang's red core is an energy tank: it spins the core gear at high speed to charge up, then fires that energy as powerful blasts of electricity through the spikes on its new gear. That spiked gear isn't actually alive, unlike the other two. Its red core may nod to the ruby jewel bearings in mechanical watches. Ken Sugimori came up with the idea for the line, and Keiko Moritsugu designed it.
description.guide: Klinklang is the final form of Klink, a Steel-type Pokémon made of interlocking gears. It stores energy in its red core and releases it through a spiked gear.
description.tagline: A clockwork machine that charges a red core and fires lightning.
